questions.question:
Which following statement is true?
a) All graphs are trees
b) All trees are graphs
c) Some trees are graphs
d) No tree is a graph
questions.explanation: Every tree is a connected acyclic graph — trees are a special case of graphs, but not all graphs are trees.

questions.question:
Which of the following is false in the case of a spanning tree of a graph G?
a) It is a tree that spans G
b) It is a sub-graph of G
c) It includes every vertex of G
d) It can be either cyclic or acyclic

options.A: It is a tree that spans G
options.B: It is a sub-graph of G
options.C: It includes every vertex of G
options.D: It can be either cyclic or acyclic

questions.explanation: A spanning tree is always acyclic by definition — it is a tree (acyclic connected subgraph) that spans all vertices of G.

questions.question:
MST full form is:
a) Maximum Spanning Tree
b) Maximum Sub Tree
c) Minimum Spanning Tree
d) Minimum Sub Tree
questions.explanation: MST stands for Minimum Spanning Tree — a spanning tree of a weighted graph with the minimum total edge weight.

questions.question:
Topological sort can be applied to which of the following graphs?
a) Undirected Cyclic Graphs
b) Directed Cyclic Graphs
c) Undirected Acyclic Graphs
d) Directed Acyclic Graphs
questions.explanation: Topological Sort is only applicable to Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) — cyclic graphs cannot have a valid topological ordering.

questions.question:
A circuit that does not repeat vertices is called ________.
a) cycle
b) path
c) tree
d) directed graph
questions.explanation: A cycle (simple circuit) is a closed path that does not repeat any vertex except the starting/ending vertex.

questions.question:
What type of approach does Prim's algorithm use to find a minimum spanning tree of a graph?
a. Divide and Conquer
b. Dynamic Programming
c. Greedy Approach
d. Backtracking
questions.explanation: Prim's algorithm uses a Greedy approach — at each step it picks the minimum weight edge that connects the growing MST to a new vertex.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true?
a) Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex
b) Prim's algorithm initializes with an edge
c) Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex which has smallest edge
d) Prim's algorithm initializes with a forest

options.A: Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex
options.B: Prim's algorithm initializes with an edge
options.C: Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex which has smallest edge
options.D: Prim's algorithm initializes with a forest

questions.explanation: Prim's algorithm starts from any arbitrary vertex and grows the MST by repeatedly adding the minimum weight edge to an unvisited vertex.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of Kruskal's algorithm (E is the number of edges and V is the number of vertices of input graph)?
a) O(log V)
b) O(E log V)
c) O(E²)
d) O(V log E)
questions.explanation: Kruskal's algorithm sorts all edges in O(E log E) and uses Union-Find for cycle detection, giving overall O(E log V) complexity.

questions.question:
Which of the following algorithms is used to find the shortest path in a graph with negative edge weights?
a. Dijkstra's Algorithm
b. Prim's Algorithm
c. Bellman-Ford Algorithm
d. Kruskal's Algorithm
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford handles negative edge weights and detects negative cycles — Dijkstra's fails with negative weights.

questions.question:
Dijkstra's algorithm is used for finding ________.
a) minimum spanning tree
b) shortest path
c) string matching
d) sorted sequence
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from a single source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph with non-negative edges.

questions.question:
Dijkstra's algorithm is known as:
a) All pair shortest path
b) All pair longest path
c) Single Source longest Path
d) Single Source shortest path
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm computes shortest paths from one source vertex to all other vertices — it is a Single Source Shortest Path algorithm.

questions.question:
Which of the following algorithms are used to find the shortest path from a source node to all other nodes in a weighted graph?
a) BFS
b) Dijkstra's Algorithm
c) Prim's Algorithm
d) Kruskal's Algorithm
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's Algorithm finds shortest paths from a single source in a weighted graph. BFS works for unweighted graphs only.

questions.question:
Floyd Warshall Algorithm used to solve the shortest path problem has a time complexity of:
a) O(VV)
b) O(VVV)
c) O(EV)
d) O(E*E)
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses three nested loops over all vertices, giving O(V³) time complexity for all-pairs shortest path.

questions.question:
What is the worst case time complexity of Prim's algorithm if adjacency matrix is used?
a) O(log V)
b) O(V²)
c) O(E²)
d) O(V log E)
questions.explanation: With an adjacency matrix, Prim's algorithm takes O(V²) — finding the minimum edge each iteration requires scanning all V vertices.

questions.question:
A graph is called a ________ if it is a connected acyclic graph.
a) cyclic graph
b) regular graph
c) tree
d) forest
questions.explanation: A connected acyclic graph is called a tree — it has exactly n-1 edges for n vertices and no cycles.

questions.question:
What is the number of edges in a tree with n nodes?
a) n
b) n-1
c) n+1
d) 2n-1
questions.explanation: A tree with n nodes always has exactly n-1 edges — adding any edge creates a cycle, removing any edge disconnects the tree.

questions.question:
DAG full form is:
a) Direct Aligned Graph
b) Direct Acyclic Graph
c) Defined Aligned Graph
d) Defined Acyclic Graph
questions.explanation: DAG stands for Directed Acyclic Graph — a directed graph with no directed cycles, used in scheduling, dependency resolution, etc.

questions.question:
What is sink in a graph?
a) A vertex with no incoming edges
b) A vertex with no outgoing edges
c) A vertex with highest degree
d) A vertex connecting two components

options.A: A vertex with no incoming edges
options.B: A vertex with no outgoing edges

questions.explanation: A sink vertex in a directed graph has no outgoing edges — its out-degree is zero.

questions.question:
Define in-degree of a graph.
a) Number of edges going out of a vertex
b) Number of edges coming into a vertex
c) Total number of edges in a graph
d) Number of vertices adjacent to a vertex

options.A: Number of edges going out of a vertex
options.B: Number of edges coming into a vertex
options.C: Total number of edges in a graph
options.D: Number of vertices adjacent to a vertex

questions.explanation: In-degree of a vertex is the number of directed edges incoming to that vertex in a directed graph.

questions.question:
What is cut vertex?
a) A vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components
b) A vertex with maximum degree
c) A vertex with minimum degree
d) A vertex with no adjacent vertices

options.A: A vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components
options.D: A vertex with no adjacent vertices

questions.explanation: A cut vertex (articulation point) is a vertex whose removal disconnects the graph — increasing the number of connected components.

questions.question:
Write one difference between path and cycle.
a) A path starts and ends at the same vertex; a cycle does not
b) A cycle starts and ends at the same vertex; a path does not
c) Both path and cycle start and end at the same vertex
d) Neither path nor cycle can repeat vertices

options.A: A path starts and ends at the same vertex; a cycle does not
options.B: A cycle starts and ends at the same vertex; a path does not
options.C: Both path and cycle start and end at the same vertex
options.D: Neither path nor cycle can repeat vertices

questions.explanation: A cycle is a closed walk that starts and ends at the same vertex; a path is an open walk from one vertex to another without repeating vertices.

Which algorithm is commonly used as the basis for Topological Sorting?
a) BFS only
b) DFS only
c) Both BFS and DFS can be used
d) Dijkstra's algorithm

options.C: Both BFS and DFS can be used

questions.explanation: Topological Sort can be implemented using DFS (post-order reversal) or BFS (Kahn's algorithm using in-degree counts).

questions.question:
Floyd-Warshall algorithm is based on which algorithm design paradigm?
a) Greedy Method
b) Divide and Conquer
c) Dynamic Programming
d) Backtracking
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses Dynamic Programming — it builds up shortest path solutions using intermediate vertices incrementally.

questions.question:
In a directed graph, each edge has:
a) No direction
b) A direction from one vertex to another
c) Two directions simultaneously
d) Direction only if it is a cycle

options.B: A direction from one vertex to another
options.D: Direction only if it is a cycle

questions.explanation: In a directed graph (digraph), each edge has an orientation — it goes from a source vertex to a destination vertex, not both ways.

questions.question:
What does Bellman-Ford algorithm do when a negative weight cycle is detected?
a) Ignores the cycle and continues
b) Reports that no shortest path exists
c) Converts negative edges to positive
d) Applies Dijkstra's algorithm instead

options.B: Reports that no shortest path exists

questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford detects negative weight cycles and reports that no shortest path solution exists, since the path cost can decrease infinitely.

a) Stack
b) Queue
c) Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
d) Priority Queue
questions.explanation: Kruskal's algorithm uses Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union) data structure to efficiently detect and avoid cycles when adding edges.

questions.question:
Why does Dijkstra's algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
a) It cannot process weighted graphs
b) It assumes all edge weights are non-negative for the greedy choice to be correct
c) It runs in infinite loops
d) It only works on undirected graphs

options.B: It assumes all edge weights are non-negative for the greedy choice to be correct
options.D: It only works on undirected graphs

questions.explanation: Dijkstra's greedy assumption — that once a vertex is visited its shortest path is finalized — breaks when negative edges can reduce path costs later.

A forest in graph theory is defined as:
a) A connected graph with cycles
b) A disconnected acyclic graph
c) A directed graph with no vertices
d) A graph where every vertex has degree 2

options.C: A directed graph with no vertices
options.D: A graph where every vertex has degree 2

questions.explanation: A forest is a collection of disjoint trees — it is an acyclic undirected graph that may not be connected (each connected component is a tree).
